key_findings_zh: 使用遭受氧化应激的分化 SH-SY5Y 细胞进行的体外研究表明,靶向 LNP 增强了细胞摄取并激活了关键的神经保护信号级联,包括 AKT、ERK 和 STAT3 磷酸化。在体内,MitoPark 小鼠鼻内给予优化的 LNP 与多巴胺能神经元标记物(如酪氨酸羟化酶)的保存和线粒体相关蛋白(如 ATP5A1)的调节趋势相关。 [10.1038/s41392-026-02897-w]
研究发现,星形胶质细胞与 CD4+ T 细胞的直接相互作用增强了实验性自身免疫性脑脊髓炎中致病性 T 辅助 17 细胞的反应。它还表明,CD4+ T 细胞的 CD40L 激活星形胶质细胞中的 CD40,导致 PLIN4 阳性脂滴的积累,从而支持 p65 乙酰化依赖性 NF-κB 激活和抗原呈递。 [10.1038/s41586-026-10860-6]
所有参与者使用 RT-PCR 检测均为阴性,表明没有检测到 狂犬病 病毒 RNA。ELISA 滴度范围为 0.881 至 4.449 IU/mL,所有参与者都超过了 0.5 IU/mL 的保护阈值。 [10.1186/s40794-026-00312-4]
基本商品的总体供应率仍低于世卫组织 80% 以上的目标,药房受到的影响比卫生中心更大。2023 年,供应量显着增加,但差异仍然存在,特别是蛇抗蛇毒血清(34.6% vs 100%)和抗狂犬病疫苗(23.1% vs 66.7%)。 [10.64898/2026.08.03.26359542]
研究发现,绝大多数人类死亡都是由狗造成的,占人类死亡的99%。 [10.21275/sr26803122405]

key_findings_zh: 格林斯博罗水街的一只浣熊 狂犬病病毒 检测呈阳性。这是吉尔福德县卫生与公众服务部公共卫生司报告的 2026 年第 11 例动物 狂犬病 确诊病例。 [news-9f695a2beb15f590]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Rabies virus news developments.
key_findings_en: A raccoon on Water Street in Greensboro tested positive for the rabies virus. This is the eleventh confirmed case of animal rabies in 2026, reported by the Guilford County Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Public Health. [news-9f695a2beb15f590]

The Indian government has mandated a new protocol for investigating suspected human rabies deaths, requiring joint teams from health, veterinary, municipal, and forest departments to trace infection sources, identify exposed contacts, and strengthen rabies surveillance under the One Health framework. [news-7bba203e48aa0065]

Sinovac Biotech received regulatory approval for a serum-free rabies vaccine, which supports a shortened four-dose vaccination schedule recommended by the World Health Organization. [news-4547d0a99ed69a7a]
A second animal tested positive for rabies in Otsego County, reported by WBNG. This is a confirmed event based on the evidence provided. [news-af5e9a0176022376]

A second beaver at Cunningham Falls State Park tested positive for rabies, as confirmed by the Maryland Department of Health. This follows a previous incident where a beaver bit a teenager on July 26, 2026, and tested positive for rabies on July 27, 2026. The event is confirmed based on official testing results. [news-db65daa7b6388ea3]

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Design Novel Peptide Inhibitors of Rabies Virus Glycoprotein
papers.abstract: Abstract Rabies is the most lethal viral zoonotic diseases worldwide. The rabies virus glycoprotein (RABV-G) which mediates host cell recognition and viral entry; it represents a therapeutic target for the development of novel anti-viral agents. In the present study, a computational peptide design strategy was employed to design peptide inhibitors against RABV-G. Peptide sequences were designed from the receptor binding region of α-bungarotoxin through mutation and optimisation while eliminating neurotoxic properties. A hybrid machine learning-deep framework was used for toxicity screening. The selected non-toxic peptides were analysed through framework of different tools for Physiochemical characterization, antiviral activity prediction, molecular docking, binding affinity and molecular dynamic simulation were performed to analyse peptide RABV-G interactions. A three-dimensional model of RABV-G was generated using SWISS MODEL and validated through Ramchandran plot analysis with 92.5% residues within favoured regions. Binding pocket analysis identified key residues involved in peptide binding including Glu272, Glu279., Asp283, Lys276 and Arg297. Among the evaluated candidates, MKMKCHTTATMKIV (P40) shown the most favourable docking with a HADDOCK scores − 90 ± 3.8, and binding free energy of -10.3kcal/mol, followed by CLDLGYTIVCHTTATSPI (P3), MKIVCHTTATSPMKV (P21), and MKIVCHTTMKSPMK (P25). Molecular dynamic simulations (100ns) analysed that P40 and P25 formed highly stable complexes with RABV-G, exhibiting low RMSD and RMSF fluctuation with intermolecular interaction, and favourable free energy landscapes and stable conformational through simulation period. This study design shows the α-bungarotoxin derived peptides can target RABV-G and P440 can be promising lead candidate for development of peptide-based drug delivery.

A computational peptide design strategy was used to generate sequences from the receptor binding region of α-bungarotoxin, optimizing them to eliminate neurotoxic properties. The study suggests that these α-bungarotoxin-derived peptides could be promising lead candidates for developing peptide-based therapies against rabies. However, the reliance on computational methods without experimental validation limits the confidence in the findings, and the evidence strength is considered moderate.

analysis_zh.methods: 使用混合机器学习深度框架进行毒性筛查。通过不同工具的框架对所选的无毒肽进行理化表征、抗病毒药物 活性预测、分子对接、结合亲和力和分子动力学模拟来分析肽 RABV-G 相互作用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在评估的候选者中,MKMKCHTTATMKIV (P40) 显示出最有利的对接,HADDOCK 得分为 − 90 ± 3.8,结合自由能为 -10.3kcal/mol,其次是 CLDLGYTIVCHTTATSPI (P3)、MKIVCHTTATSPMKV (P21) 和 MKIVCHTTMKSPMK (P25)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究设计表明,α-金环蛇毒素衍生肽可以靶向 RABV-G,而 P440 可能成为开发基于肽的药物递送的有前途的主要候选药物。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发针对 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白的基于肽的药物递送系统提供信息,从而有可能为 狂犬病 感染带来新的治疗策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算方法,不包括实验验证,这限制了结果的可信度。由于依赖计算机分析,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Peptide-targeted cubosome and hexosome nanoassemblies mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a MitoPark model.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a primary pathogenic mechanism underlying dopaminergic neuron loss in the nigrostriatal pathway in Parkinson's disease (PD). To investigate mitochondrion-targeted therapeutic strategies, we utilized the MitoPark mouse model, in which mitochondrial transcription factor A (Tfam) is selectively ablated in midbrain dopamine neurons, resulting in progressive neurodegeneration. We designed multifunctional lyotropic liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) of the cubosome and hexosome types for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery. These nanocarriers were engineered with lipids essential for membrane integrity (plasmalogens and ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs)) and a nonlamellar structural lipid (monoolein). They coencapsulated the neuroprotective antioxidants ginkgolide B and quercetin. To facilitate neuronal targeting and uptake, the surface of the LCNP was modified by conjugation with pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) and a rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-derived peptide-oleic acid (RVG-OL) conjugate. In vitro studies using differentiated SH-SY5Y cells subjected to oxidative stress demonstrated that the targeted LNPs enhanced cellular uptake and activated key neuroprotective signaling cascades, including AKT, ERK, and STAT3 phosphorylation. In vivo, intranasal administration of the optimized LNPs in MitoPark mice was associated with a trend toward the preservation of dopaminergic neuronal markers (such as tyrosine hydroxylase) and the regulation of mitochondrial-related proteins such as ATP5A1. Transcriptomic profiling revealed extensive molecular reprogramming. The peptide-functionalized LNPs upregulated genes enriched in mitochondrial biogenesis (Ppargc1a and Pink1) and survival (Bcl2) but downregulated the expression of neuroinflammatory mediators (Il6, Nos2, Myd88, and Trem2) and apoptotic effectors. These findings establish peptide-targeted, therapeutic lipid (plasmalogen/PUFA)-based nanoassemblies as a potent nonviral platform for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery that may modulate mitochondrial- and neurodegeneration-related signaling pathways in a genetic model of PD.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of peptide-targeted nanoassemblies to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a Parkinson's disease model. The researchers designed cubosome and hexosome nanoparticles with specific lipids and neuroprotective agents to enhance neuronal uptake and activation of protective signaling pathways. In vitro and in vivo results showed improved cellular uptake and trends toward preservation of dopaminergic markers and regulation of mitochondrial proteins. The findings suggest these nanoassemblies could be a promising nonviral platform for targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases. However, the study's reliance on animal models limits its direct applicability to human conditions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 线粒体功能障碍是帕金森病 (PD) 黑质纹状体通路中多巴胺能神经元丢失的主要致病机制。该研究旨在探索线粒体靶向治疗策略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用 MitoPark 小鼠模型,其中中脑多巴胺神经元中的线粒体转录因子 A (Tfam) 被选择性消除,导致进行性神经变性。该研究的重点是评估该模型中肽靶向纳米组件的效果。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员设计了立方体和六体类型的多功能溶致液晶纳米颗粒(LCNP),用于无创鼻到脑输送。这些纳米载体采用对膜完整性至关重要的脂质(缩醛磷脂和 ω-3 多不饱和脂肪酸 (PUFA))和非层状结构脂质(单油酸甘油酯)进行设计。
elements_zh.main_results: 使用遭受氧化应激的分化 SH-SY5Y 细胞进行的体外研究表明,靶向 LNP 增强了细胞摄取并激活了关键的神经保护信号级联,包括 AKT、ERK 和 STAT3 磷酸化。在体内,MitoPark 小鼠鼻内给予优化的 LNP 与多巴胺能神经元标记物(如酪氨酸羟化酶)的保存和线粒体相关蛋白(如 ATP5A1)的调节趋势相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,基于肽靶向、治疗性脂质(缩醛磷脂/PUFA)的纳米组件可以作为一种有效的非病毒平台,用于无创鼻到脑递送,可以调节帕金森病遗传模型中线粒体和神经变性相关的信号通路。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究提供了关于非病毒纳米组装体调节帕金森病线粒体功能障碍和神经变性的潜力的见解,这可以为未来的治疗策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖体外和体内模型而受到限制,这些模型可能无法完全代表人类状况。由于缺乏直接的临床结果,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 肽靶向立方体和六糖体纳米组件可减轻 MitoPark 模型中的线粒体功能障碍。
papers.source_body_en: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a primary pathogenic mechanism underlying dopaminergic neuron loss in the nigrostriatal pathway in Parkinson's disease (PD). To investigate mitochondrion-targeted therapeutic strategies, we utilized the MitoPark mouse model, in which mitochondrial transcription factor A (Tfam) is selectively ablated in midbrain dopamine neurons, resulting in progressive neurodegeneration. We designed multifunctional lyotropic liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) of the cubosome and hexosome types for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery. These nanocarriers were engineered with lipids essential for membrane integrity (plasmalogens and ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs)) and a nonlamellar structural lipid (monoolein). They coencapsulated the neuroprotective antioxidants ginkgolide B and quercetin. To facilitate neuronal targeting and uptake, the surface of the LCNP was modified by conjugation with pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) and a rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-derived peptide-oleic acid (RVG-OL) conjugate. In vitro studies using differentiated SH-SY5Y cells subjected to oxidative stress demonstrated that the targeted LNPs enhanced cellular uptake and activated key neuroprotective signaling cascades, including AKT, ERK, and STAT3 phosphorylation. In vivo, intranasal administration of the optimized LNPs in MitoPark mice was associated with a trend toward the preservation of dopaminergic neuronal markers (such as tyrosine hydroxylase) and the regulation of mitochondrial-related proteins such as ATP5A1. Transcriptomic profiling revealed extensive molecular reprogramming. The peptide-functionalized LNPs upregulated genes enriched in mitochondrial biogenesis (Ppargc1a and Pink1) and survival (Bcl2) but downregulated the expression of neuroinflammatory mediators (Il6, Nos2, Myd88, and Trem2) and apoptotic effectors. These findings establish peptide-targeted, therapeutic lipid (plasmalogen/PUFA)-based nanoassemblies as a potent nonviral platform for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery that may modulate mitochondrial- and neurodegeneration-related signaling pathways in a genetic model of PD.

papers.title: Environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing for post-elimination surveillance of neglected tropical diseases in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region
papers.abstract: Post-elimination surveillance remains one of the most difficult challenges in neglected tropical disease (NTD) control. As countries in the Western Pacific Region approach elimination targets, conventional diagnostic tools such as microscopy and antigen rapid tests, optimised for moderate-to-high prevalence settings, are insufficient to detect the rare, focal, or reintroduced transmission that characterises near-elimination settings. The WHO Global Report on Neglected Tropical Diseases 2025 identifies weak surveillance systems and insufficient diagnostic innovation as primary threats to sustaining gains toward the 2030 road map, yet no operational framework exists for deploying environmental genomic surveillance in resource-limited post-elimination settings. The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated the transformative potential of next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based wastewater surveillance for population-level pathogen detection, yet environmental NGS remains substantially underused for NTDs. In the Philippines, where lymphatic filariasis and Schistosoma japonicum approach elimination while soil-transmitted helminthiases, foodborne trematodes and rabies persist at low, focal prevalence, climate-driven rainfall and flooding concentrate pathogen burden within specific watersheds, drainage systems and habitats. Effective surveillance therefore requires frameworks that go beyond assay sensitivity and specificity to address how surveillance objectives, low-prevalence conditions, sampling strategy, and resource constraints jointly determine what can realistically be detected. This narrative review synthesises evidence on targeted and metagenomic NGS across the three locations in which an NTD signal can be recovered: environmental matrices, vectors and intermediate hosts, and animal reservoirs, using lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, rabies, and related NTDs in the Philippines as a case example. We organise diseases by transmission route and the resulting signal location, which together determine the sampling matrix and the appropriate NGS approach (metabarcoding versus shotgun metagenomics). We argue that the principal remaining gap is not detection but integration: calibrating the environmental signal to infection prevalence and linking it with vector, host and clinical data to guide programmatic decisions, aligned with the 2030 NTD road map.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, with an emphasis on post-elimination surveillance strategies in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region. The central question is how to effectively detect and monitor rabies in low-prevalence, focal transmission settings using environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of evidence on targeted and metagenomic NGS approaches for detecting rabies virus in environmental matrices, vectors, intermediate hosts, and animal reservoirs. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods, but it outlines the general framework for integrating NGS with surveillance objectives and resource constraints.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that environmental NGS has the potential to transform post-elimination rabies surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings. It highlights the need for frameworks that go beyond assay sensitivity and specificity to address how surveillance objectives, low-prevalence conditions, sampling strategy, and resource constraints jointly determine what can realistically be detected.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a key gap in the integration of environmental signals with infection prevalence and other biological data. It also notes that while NGS-based wastewater surveillance has shown promise during the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental NGS remains underutilized for neglected tropical diseases like rabies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing operational frameworks for deploying environmental genomic surveillance in post-elimination settings. It also highlights the importance of linking environmental signals with vector, host, and clinical data to guide programmatic decisions aligned with the 2030 NTD road map.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for post-elimination rabies surveillance in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region. It identifies the limitations of conventional diagnostic tools in low-prevalence settings and argues for the need of integrated frameworks that combine NGS with surveillance objectives and resource constraints. The review highlights the potential of NGS-based wastewater surveillance, as demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic, but notes its underutilization for rabies. It emphasizes the importance of calibrating environmental signals with infection prevalence and other biological data to support programmatic decisions in line with the 2030 NTD road map.

The central question is how to effectively detect and monitor rabies in low-prevalence, focal transmission settings using environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of evidence on targeted and metagenomic NGS approaches for detecting rabies virus in environmental matrices, vectors, intermediate hosts, and animal reservoirs. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods, but it outlines the general framework for integrating NGS with surveillance objectives and resource constraints.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that environmental NGS has the potential to transform post-elimination rabies surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings. It highlights the need for frameworks that go beyond assay sensitivity and specificity to address how surveillance objectives, low-prevalence conditions, sampling strategy, and resource constraints jointly determine what can realistically be detected.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a key gap in the integration of environmental signals with infection prevalence and other biological data. It also notes that while NGS-based wastewater surveillance has shown promise during the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental NGS remains underutilized for neglected tropical diseases like rabies.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing operational frameworks for deploying environmental genomic surveillance in post-elimination settings. It also highlights the importance of linking environmental signals with vector, host, and clinical data to guide programmatic decisions aligned with the 2030 NTD road map.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对用于检测环境基质中的 狂犬病病毒、媒介、中间体 宿主 和动物 储存宿主 的靶向和宏基因组 NGS 方法证据的叙述性综合。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期或荟萃分析方法,但概述了将 NGS 与 监测 目标和资源限制相集成的总体框架。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,环境 NGS 有潜力改变消除后 狂犬病 监测,特别是在资源有限的环境中。它强调需要超越检测灵敏度和特异性的框架,以解决 监测 目标、低 患病率 条件、采样策略和资源限制如何共同确定可以实际检测到的内容。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了环境信号与感染 患病率 和其他生物数据整合方面的关键差距。它还指出,虽然基于 NGS 的废水 监测 在 COVID-19 大流行期间显示出希望,但环境 NGS 在治疗 狂犬病 等被忽视的热带疾病方面仍未得到充分利用。

papers.title_zh: 菲律宾和西太平洋区域被忽视的热带病消除后 监测 的环境 DNA 和下一代测序
papers.source_body_en: Post-elimination surveillance remains one of the most difficult challenges in neglected tropical disease (NTD) control. As countries in the Western Pacific Region approach elimination targets, conventional diagnostic tools such as microscopy and antigen rapid tests, optimised for moderate-to-high prevalence settings, are insufficient to detect the rare, focal, or reintroduced transmission that characterises near-elimination settings. The WHO Global Report on Neglected Tropical Diseases 2025 identifies weak surveillance systems and insufficient diagnostic innovation as primary threats to sustaining gains toward the 2030 road map, yet no operational framework exists for deploying environmental genomic surveillance in resource-limited post-elimination settings. The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated the transformative potential of next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based wastewater surveillance for population-level pathogen detection, yet environmental NGS remains substantially underused for NTDs. In the Philippines, where lymphatic filariasis and Schistosoma japonicum approach elimination while soil-transmitted helminthiases, foodborne trematodes and rabies persist at low, focal prevalence, climate-driven rainfall and flooding concentrate pathogen burden within specific watersheds, drainage systems and habitats. Effective surveillance therefore requires frameworks that go beyond assay sensitivity and specificity to address how surveillance objectives, low-prevalence conditions, sampling strategy, and resource constraints jointly determine what can realistically be detected. This narrative review synthesises evidence on targeted and metagenomic NGS across the three locations in which an NTD signal can be recovered: environmental matrices, vectors and intermediate hosts, and animal reservoirs, using lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, rabies, and related NTDs in the Philippines as a case example. We organise diseases by transmission route and the resulting signal location, which together determine the sampling matrix and the appropriate NGS approach (metabarcoding versus shotgun metagenomics). We argue that the principal remaining gap is not detection but integration: calibrating the environmental signal to infection prevalence and linking it with vector, host and clinical data to guide programmatic decisions, aligned with the 2030 NTD road map.
papers.abstract_zh: 消除后 监测 仍然是被忽视的热带病 (NTD) 控制中最困难的挑战之一。随着西太平洋区域国家接近消除目标,针对中至高 患病率 设置进行优化的传统诊断工具(例如显微镜和抗原快速检测)不足以检测到接近消除设置的罕见、局部或重新引入的 传播。世卫组织《2025 年被忽视的热带病全球报告》将薄弱的 监测 系统和不足的诊断创新确定为维持 2030 年路线图成果的主要威胁,但在资源有限的消灭后环境中部署环境 基因组监测 的操作框架尚不存在。COVID-19 大流行证明了基于下一代测序 (NGS) 的废水 监测 在人群水平病原体检测方面的变革潜力,但环境 NGS 在检测 NTD 方面仍然大大未得到充分利用。在菲律宾,淋巴丝虫病和日本血吸虫病已接近消除,而土源性蠕虫病、食源性吸虫和 狂犬病 持续处于低水平、局灶性 狂犬病 状态,气候驱动的降雨和洪水使特定流域、排水系统和栖息地内的病原体负担集中。因此,有效的 监测 需要超越检测灵敏度和特异性的框架,以解决 监测 目标、低 患病率 条件、采样策略和资源限制如何共同确定可以实际检测到的内容。这篇叙述性综述综合了可恢复 NTD 信号的三个位置的靶向和宏基因组 NGS 的证据:环境基质、媒介 和中间 宿主 以及动物 储存宿主,并以菲律宾的淋巴丝虫病、血吸虫病、狂犬病 和相关 NTD 作为案例。我们通过 传播 途径和由此产生的信号位置来组织疾病,它们共同确定采样矩阵和适当的 NGS 方法(元条形码与鸟枪法宏基因组学)。我们认为,剩下的主要差距不是检测,而是整合:校准感染 患病率 的环境信号,并将其与 媒介、宿主 和临床数据联系起来,以指导规划决策,与 2030 年 NTD 路线图保持一致。

papers.title: Determinants of rabies knowledge, attitudes, and practices among secondary and vocational school students in Maha Sarakham Province, Thailand
papers.abstract: Abstract Rabies is a critical zoonotic disease that is found throughout the world, particularly in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Once a clinical sign appears, the fatality rate rises to 100% globally. In Thailand, children under the age of 15 had the highest annual reported exposure rate to rabies infection. One of the most significant barriers to disease prevention and control is a lack of public awareness about rabies, particularly among children and young people. The study’s goal was to determine knowledge, attitude, and preventive practice (KAP) about rabies and associated factors among secondary and vocational students in Maha Sarakham, Thailand, in 2023. An analytic cross-sectional survey was carried out from January to May 2023, with a total of 628 study participants. Data was collected through online and on-site questionnaires. Descriptive analysis was carried out. Inferential statistics analysis was also performed to identify factors associated with rabies KAP among the target participants. Most participants demonstrated a moderate level of knowledge (55.89%), neutral attitudes (81.37%), and moderate preventive practices (72.77%) toward rabies. Students who had experience raising animals, had previously studied zoonotic diseases, had a history of animal bites or scratches, or had received rabies vaccination showed significantly higher knowledge and practice scores ( p < 0.05). Knowledge and attitudes were positively correlated with preventive practices ( r = 0.14 and r = 0.28, respectively; p < 0.05). The findings suggest a significant need for rabies awareness programs targeting school and college students within the community. The materials designed to promote KAP regarding rabies should address specific topics, including the risk of rabies, modes of transmission, the significance of first aid, health-seeking behavior following dog bites or cat scratches, and preventive measures for both pets and community dogs and cats.

papers.title: Primary healthcare facilities readiness for animal-related injuries: Availability, stock-Outs, and affordability of essential commodities in rural public health facilities, Tanzania
papers.abstract: Abstract Background In Tanzania, reported cases for animal-related injuries is approximated to be 200-40,000, where most of deaths and complications from these cases are entirely preventable when safe, affordable and effective medications are available and administered in a timely manner. Methodology/Principal findings This study analyzed the availability, stockouts, and affordability of essential animal-related injury health commodities at primary healthcare (PHC) facilities in rural settings in Tanzania. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in February 2024, using health facility data covering the period from 2019 to 2023. Availability, stockouts, and price of the selected 33 health commodities were extracted from hospital pharmaceutical ledgers at 29 selected public PHC facilities in Mkinga District, Tanga region comprising 26 dispensaries and three health centers. Affordability was calculated using the wage of the lowest-paid government worker per day approach. Overall availability remained below the WHO target of > 80% and dispensaries were more affected than health centers. Notable incremental availability was observed in 2023; however, differences were observed between dispensaries and health centers; snake antivenom (34.6% vs 100%), antirabies (23.1% vs 66.7%), adrenaline injection (73.1% vs 100%), and dexamethasone injection (0% vs 66.7%). Across the five years, dispensaries had more stockouts between 2019 and 2021, reporting up to a 53.8% stockout rate for chlorpheniramine tablets, with the longest stockout period of 218 days for an IV giving set in 2019. The health centers had higher stockouts between 2021 and 2022, reporting up to a 66.7% stockout rate for hydrocortisone injection in 2021 and the longest stockout period of 102 days for dexamethasone injection in 2020. Using the affordability threshold of 7% of daily income for healthcare expenditure, nearly all assessed commodities were classified as unaffordable. Conclusions/Significance Essential commodities for managing animal-related injuries remain inadequately available, frequently out of stock, and largely unaffordable in rural PHC facilities in Tanzania, particularly anti-rabies biologicals and snake antivenom. Strengthening surveillance, forecasting, procurement, financing, and supply chain systems, alongside expanding financial risk protection through health insurance and targeted subsidies, is essential to improve equitable access to life-saving commodities. Author Summary Most of deaths and complications from animal-related cases are entirely preventable when safe, affordable and effective medications are available and administered in a timely manner. In this study we analyzed availability, stockout and affordability of the of essential animal-related injury health commodities at primary healthcare facilities in rural settings in Tanzania. Essential health commodities for managing animal-related injuries were available below the WHO-recommended target, with anti-rabies biologicals and snake antivenoms showing the poorest availability. Frequent and prolonged stockouts, particularly in dispensaries, substantially limited continuous access to life-saving medicines and medical supplies for animal-related injuries. Nearly all assessed commodities were unaffordable using the lowest-paid government worker benchmark, highlighting the need to strengthen supply chain systems, forecasting, and sustainable financing to improve equitable access.

source_records.title: Primary healthcare facilities readiness for animal-related injuries: Availability, stock-Outs, and affordability of essential commodities in rural public health facilities, Tanzania
source_records.abstract: Background In Tanzania, reported cases for animal-related injuries is approximated to be 200-40,000, where most of deaths and complications from these cases are entirely preventable when safe, affordable and effective medications are available and administered in a timely manner. Methodology/Principal findings This study analyzed the availability, stockouts, and affordability of essential animal-related injury health commodities at primary healthcare (PHC) facilities in rural settings in Tanzania. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in February 2024, using health facility data covering the period from 2019 to 2023. Availability, stockouts, and price of the selected 33 health commodities were extracted from hospital pharmaceutical ledgers at 29 selected public PHC facilities in Mkinga District, Tanga region comprising 26 dispensaries and three health centers. Affordability was calculated using the wage of the lowest-paid government worker per day approach. Overall availability remained below the WHO target of > 80% and dispensaries were more affected than health centers. Notable incremental availability was observed in 2023; however, differences were observed between dispensaries and health centers; snake antivenom (34.6% vs 100%), antirabies (23.1% vs 66.7%), adrenaline injection (73.1% vs 100%), and dexamethasone injection (0% vs 66.7%). Across the five years, dispensaries had more stockouts between 2019 and 2021, reporting up to a 53.8% stockout rate for chlorpheniramine tablets, with the longest stockout period of 218 days for an IV giving set in 2019. The health centers had higher stockouts between 2021 and 2022, reporting up to a 66.7% stockout rate for hydrocortisone injection in 2021 and the longest stockout period of 102 days for dexamethasone injection in 2020. Using the affordability threshold of 7% of daily income for healthcare expenditure, nearly all assessed commodities were classified as unaffordable. Conclusions/Significance Essential commodities for managing animal-related injuries remain inadequately available, frequently out of stock, and largely unaffordable in rural PHC facilities in Tanzania, particularly anti-rabies biologicals and snake antivenom. Strengthening surveillance, forecasting, procurement, financing, and supply chain systems, alongside expanding financial risk protection through health insurance and targeted subsidies, is essential to improve equitable access to life-saving commodities.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在坦桑尼亚,报告的动物相关伤害病例约为 200-40,000 例,如果能够及时获得并及时使用安全、负担得起且有效的药物,则这些病例造成的大多数死亡和并发症是完全可以预防的。方法/主要结果 本研究分析了坦桑尼亚农村地区初级医疗保健 (PHC) 设施中与动物相关的基本伤害保健商品的可用性、缺货情况和可负担性。2024 年 2 月进行了一项回顾性横断面研究,使用了 2019 年至 2023 年期间的卫生设施数据。从坦噶地区姆金加区 29 个选定的公共初级卫生保健设施(包括 26 个药房和三个卫生中心)的医院药品分类账中提取了选定的 33 种卫生用品的供应情况、缺货情况和价格。负担能力是使用最低工资政府工作人员每日工资的方法计算的。总体可用性仍低于世卫组织 80% 以上的目标,而且药房比卫生中心受到的影响更大。2023 年可用性显着增加;然而,药房和保健中心之间存在差异;抗蛇毒血清(34.6% vs 100%)、抗狂犬病(23.1% vs 66.7%)、肾上腺素注射(73.1% vs 100%)和地塞米松注射(0% vs 66.7%)。过去五年中,药房在 2019 年至 2021 年期间缺货较多,报告称扑尔敏片剂的缺货率高达 53.8%,其中 2019 年静脉注射的最长缺货期为 218 天。卫生中心在 2021 年至 2022 年期间缺货率更高,报告称 2021 年氢化可的松注射液的缺货率高达 66.7%,地塞米松注射液2020年最长缺货期为102天。以医疗保健支出占日收入7%的负担能力门槛,几乎所有评估商品都被列为难以负担。结论/意义 坦桑尼亚农村初级卫生保健设施中用于管理动物相关伤害的基本商品仍然供应不足、经常缺货,而且基本上难以负担,特别是抗 狂犬病 生物制剂和抗蛇毒血清。加强监测、预测、采购、融资和供应链系统,同时通过健康保险和定向补贴扩大金融风险保护,对于改善救生商品的公平获取至关重要。作者摘要 如果能够及时获得并使用安全、负担得起且有效的药物,则大多数动物相关病例的死亡和并发症是完全可以预防的。在这项研究中,我们分析了坦桑尼亚农村地区初级卫生保健机构与动物相关的基本伤害保健商品的可用性、缺货情况和可负担性。用于管理动物相关伤害的基本卫生用品的供应量低于世卫组织建议的目标,其中抗 狂犬病 生物制剂和蛇抗蛇毒血清的供应量最差。频繁且长期的缺货,特别是在药房,严重限制了救生药物和动物相关伤害医疗用品的持续获取。使用最低工资的政府工作人员基准,几乎所有评估的商品都是难以承受的,这凸显出需要加强供应链系统、预测和可持续融资,以改善公平准入。

papers.title: Antigen presentation by CD40+MHC-II+ astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity.
papers.abstract: Astrocytes contribute to the pathology of multiple neurological disorders, including the T cell-driven autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS) multiple sclerosis and its mouse model, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis 1 . However, little is known about functional interactions between astrocytes and CD4 + T cells. Here using rabies barcode interaction detection followed by sequencing 2 , in combination with single-cell RNA sequencing, in vitro co-culture systems and cell-specific in vivo CRISPR-Cas9-based genetic perturbation studies, we established that astrocytes expressing CD40 and MHC-II promote CNS T cell autoimmunity. papers.title: Rabies viral RNA and antibody response after post-exposure prophylaxis: Implications for blood donor deferral
papers.abstract: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) using anti-rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin is widely recognized as highly effective. However, individuals who receive PEP are typically deferred from blood donation for a full year, largely due to theoretical concerns about transfusion safety. However, the evidence supporting such a prolonged deferral remains limited. This study aimed to assess rabies real-time RT-PCR status and serological responses among PEP recipients at various intervals following treatment and to consider whether these findings might justify a re-examination of the current one-year blood donor deferral policy after anti-rabies treatment. We conducted a single-center interventional study at an anti-rabies clinic in a tertiary hospital in North India. The study enrolled twenty immunologically naïve adults who had sustained category III animal bites, with no prior rabies exposure or treatment, and who adhered fully to the protocol. Participants received anti-rabies vaccines and equine rabies immunoglobulin as appropriate for their category. Follow-up samples were collected between as early as 48 days and 120 days after the bites. These samples were tested for rabies viral RNA using real-time RT-PCR (Geno-Sens Rabies Real-Time PCR Kit), and antibody titers were measured using ELISA (Rabies Platelia Kit II). Data analysis included descriptive statistics, percentile analysis, correlation analysis, and regression analysis, as appropriate. In this cohort, dogs were responsible for 90% of bites, with 85% of incidents being unprovoked and 65% involving lower limbs. All participants tested negative using RT-PCR. ELISA titers ranged from 0.881 to 4.449 IU/mL, and all participants exceeded the protective threshold of 0.5 IU/mL. The mean titer was 2.97 ± 1.04 IU/mL. The lack of detectable rabies viral RNA, together with sustained protective antibody titers, indicates an effective response to PEP in this group. These findings support a more evidence-based reconsideration of the current prolonged blood donor deferral following anti-rabies treatment. Rabies remains a major public health concern in India, where most human exposures occur after animal bites, especially dog bites. Post-exposure prophylaxis using anti-rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin is highly effective when given correctly. However, people who receive anti-rabies treatment are often deferred from blood donation for one year, mainly because of theoretical concerns about transfusion safety. Evidence supporting such a long deferral period is limited. In this study, we followed 20 immunologically naïve adults with category III animal bites who received standard anti-rabies post-exposure prophylaxis. Blood samples were collected 48 to 120 days after exposure and tested for rabies viral RNA using real-time RT-PCR and for rabies antibody levels using ELISA. All participants were RT-PCR negative, indicating no detectable rabies viral RNA. All also had antibody levels above the accepted protective threshold. These findings suggest that individuals who complete appropriate anti-rabies post-exposure prophylaxis may not have detectable circulating viral RNA and maintain protective antibody responses during follow-up. Larger multicenter studies are needed, but these results support reconsideration of the current one-year blood donor deferral. Our findings suggest the potential for shortening the current one-year deferral for PEP recipients, supporting evidence-based transfusion policies after anti-rabies treatment.

papers.abstract_zh: 狂犬病 暴露后预防(PEP)使用抗狂犬病 疫苗和免疫球蛋白被广泛认为是高效的。然而,接受 PEP 的个人通常会推迟一整年才献血,这主要是由于理论上对输血安全的担忧。然而,支持如此长时间推迟的证据仍然有限。本研究旨在评估 狂犬病 后不同时间间隔的 PEP 接受者的 狂犬病 实时 RT-PCR 状态和血清学反应,并考虑这些结果是否可以证明在抗 狂犬病 治疗 后重新审查当前一年的献血者延期政策是合理的。我们在印度北部一家三级医院的抗 狂犬病 诊所进行了单中心介入研究。该研究招募了 20 名免疫学上未接受过 III 类动物咬伤的成年人,他们之前没有接触过 狂犬病 或 治疗,并且完全遵守该方案。参与者接受了适合其类别的抗 狂犬病 疫苗 和马 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白。追踪样本是在被咬后 48 天到 120 天之间收集的。使用实时 RT-PCR(Geno-Sens 狂犬病 实时 PCR 试剂盒)测试这些样本的 狂犬病 病毒 RNA,并使用 ELISA(狂犬病 Platelia 试剂盒 II)测量抗体滴度。数据分析酌情包括描述性统计、百分位数分析、相关性分析和回归分析。在本次队列研究中,狗咬伤事件占90%,其中85%是无端事件,65%涉及下肢。所有参与者使用 RT-PCR 检测均为阴性。ELISA 滴度范围为 0.881 至 4.449 IU/mL,所有参与者都超过了 0.5 IU/mL 的保护阈值。平均滴度为 2.97 ± 1.04 IU/mL。缺乏可检测到的 狂犬病 病毒 RNA,以及持续的保护性抗体滴度,表明该组中对 PEP 的有效反应。这些发现支持对当前抗 狂犬病 治疗 后延长献血者延期进行更有依据的重新考虑。狂犬病 仍然是印度的一个主要公共卫生问题,大多数人类暴露发生在动物咬伤(尤其是狗咬伤)之后。如果正确给予,使用抗 狂犬病 疫苗 和 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白的 暴露后预防 是非常有效的。然而,接受抗 狂犬病 治疗 的人通常会推迟一年献血,主要是因为理论上对输血安全的担忧。支持如此长的推迟期的证据是有限的。在这项研究中,我们跟踪了 20 名未接受过免疫学治疗、被 III 类动物咬伤的成年人,他们接受了标准抗 狂犬病 暴露后预防 治疗。暴露后 48 至 120 天收集血样,并使用实时 RT-PCR 检测 狂犬病 病毒 RNA,并使用 ELISA 检测 狂犬病 抗体水平。所有参与者的 RT-PCR 均为阴性,表明没有检测到 狂犬病 病毒 RNA。所有患者的抗体水平都高于公认的保护阈值。这些发现表明,完成适当的抗 狂犬病 暴露后预防 的个体可能没有可检测到的循环病毒 RNA,并在随访期间维持保护性抗体反应。需要更大规模的多中心研究,但这些结果支持重新考虑当前一年的献血者延期。我们的研究结果表明,有可能缩短 PEP 接受者当前一年的延期,支持抗 狂犬病 治疗 后基于证据的输血政策。

papers.title: Exposure Sources and Anatomical Sites of Animal Bite and Scratch Injury Visits in Urban Hangzhou, China: A Retrospective Visit-Level Study, 2017-2020
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Animal bite and scratch injuries are common presentations to rabies-prevention clinics. Although rabies is preventable through timely wound care and post-exposure prophylaxis, routine hospital data are often underused for identifying local epidemiological patterns and prevention priorities. Objective To describe the epidemiological characteristics of animal bite and scratch injuries treated in a large urban hospital in Hangzhou, China, and to identify routinely recorded factors associated with WHO category III exposure. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 38,537 visit records from the Binjiang District Campus of the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The dataset covered 1 January 2017 to 27 October 2020. Variables included sex, age, preliminary diagnosis, triage grade, exposure grade, exposure site, and visit date derived from the triage serial number. Exposure source and injury mechanism were classified from diagnosis keywords. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests with Cramer's V, and multivariable logistic regression were used. The unit of analysis was the visit record. Results Among all records, 21,515 (55.8%) were female and the mean age was 30.5 ± 14.4 years. Cat-related injuries accounted for 19,137 records (49.7%), followed by dog-related injuries (16,844, 43.7%). Bite and scratch injuries were almost equally represented (19,025 [49.4%] and 19,172 [49.7%], respectively). Among 38,439 records with valid exposure grading, category II exposure predominated (33,214, 86.4%), whereas category III exposure represented 2,456 cases (6.4%). Upper-limb injuries were most common (28,180, 73.3% of valid site records). Visits increased from 6,934 in 2017 to 12,131 in 2019; 2020 data were incomplete. Monthly visits peaked in July and August. analysis.research_question_and_background: Animal bite and scratch injuries are common presentations to rabies-prevention clinics. Although rabies is preventable through timely wound care and post-exposure prophylaxis, routine hospital data are often underused for identifying local epidemiological patterns and prevention priorities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 38,537 visit records from the Binjiang District Campus of the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The dataset covered 1 January 2017 to 27 October 2020. Variables included sex, age, preliminary diagnosis, triage grade, exposure grade, exposure site, and visit date derived from the triage serial number.
analysis.methods: Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests with Cramer's V, and multivariable logistic regression were used. Exposure source and injury mechanism were classified from diagnosis keywords. The unit of analysis was the visit record.
analysis.main_results: Among all records, 21,515 (55.8%) were female and the mean age was 30.5 ± 14.4 years. Cat-related injuries accounted for 19,137 records (49.7%), followed by dog-related injuries (16,844, 43.7%). Bite and scratch injuries were almost equally represented (19,025 [49.4%] and 19,172 [49.7%], respectively). Among the examined variables, exposure grade showed the most evident association with anatomical site, although the effect size was small (Cramer's V = 0.118, p.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides a detailed description of the epidemiological characteristics of animal bite and scratch injuries in a large urban hospital in Hangzhou, China, and identifies routinely recorded factors associated with WHO category III exposure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform local rabies prevention strategies by highlighting the most common sources and sites of animal bite and scratch injuries, which may guide targeted interventions and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for missing data, particularly in 2020. The evidence is moderate as it relies on routine hospital records and does not include direct virological testing for rabies virus.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 38,537 visit records from a large urban hospital in Hangzhou, China, to describe the epidemiological characteristics of animal bite and scratch injuries and identify factors associated with WHO category III exposure. The dataset covered 2017-2020, with visits increasing over time. Cat-related injuries were most common, followed by dog-related injuries, and bite and scratch injuries were almost equally represented. The study found that exposure grade was most associated with anatomical site, though the effect size was small. The findings highlight the need for targeted rabies prevention strategies based on local patterns of injury sources and sites. However, the study's retrospective design and incomplete 2020 data limit its evidence strength, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 动物咬伤和抓伤是 狂犬病 预防诊所的常见症状。尽管 狂犬病 可以通过及时的伤口护理和 暴露后预防 来预防,但常规医院数据通常没有充分利用来确定当地的流行病学模式和预防重点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对浙江大学医学院附属第二医院滨江院区的 38,537 条就诊记录进行了回顾性横断面分析。该数据集涵盖2017年1月1日至2020年10月27日。变量包括性别、年龄、初步诊断、分诊等级、暴露等级、暴露部位以及从分诊序列号得出的就诊日期。
elements_zh.methods: 使用了描述性统计、Cramer V 的卡方检验和多变量逻辑回归。根据诊断关键词对暴露源和损伤机制进行分类。分析单位是访问记录。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有记录中,21,515 名(55.8%)为女性,平均年龄为 30.5 ± 14.4 岁。与猫相关的伤害占 19,137 条记录(49.7%),其次是与狗相关的伤害(16,844 条,43.7%)。咬伤和抓伤的比例几乎相同(分别为 19,025 例 [49.4%] 和 19,172 例 [49.7%])。在检查的变量中,暴露等级显示出与解剖部位最明显的关联,尽管效应大小很小(Cramer's V = 0.118,p. 11)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究详细描述了中国杭州一家大型城市医院中动物咬伤和抓伤的流行病学特征,并确定了与世界卫生组织 III 类接触相关的常规记录因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调动物咬伤和抓伤的最常见来源和部位,为当地的 狂犬病 预防策略提供信息,从而指导有针对性的干预措施和资源分配。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的数据缺失而受到限制,尤其是在 2020 年。该研究的证据是中等的,因为它依赖于常规医院记录,并且不包括 狂犬病病毒 的直接病毒学检测。

Objective To describe the epidemiological characteristics of animal bite and scratch injuries treated in a large urban hospital in Hangzhou, China, and to identify routinely recorded factors associated with WHO category III exposure. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 38,537 visit records from the Binjiang District Campus of the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The dataset covered 1 January 2017 to 27 October 2020. Variables included sex, age, preliminary diagnosis, triage grade, exposure grade, exposure site, and visit date derived from the triage serial number. Exposure source and injury mechanism were classified from diagnosis keywords. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests with Cramer's V, and multivariable logistic regression were used. The unit of analysis was the visit record. Results Among all records, 21,515 (55.8%) were female and the mean age was 30.5 ± 14.4 years. Cat-related injuries accounted for 19,137 records (49.7%), followed by dog-related injuries (16,844, 43.7%). Bite and scratch injuries were almost equally represented (19,025 [49.4%] and 19,172 [49.7%], respectively). Among 38,439 records with valid exposure grading, category II exposure predominated (33,214, 86.4%), whereas category III exposure represented 2,456 cases (6.4%). Upper-limb injuries were most common (28,180, 73.3% of valid site records). Visits increased from 6,934 in 2017 to 12,131 in 2019; 2020 data were incomplete. Monthly visits peaked in July and August. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 动物咬伤和抓伤是 狂犬病 预防诊所的常见症状。尽管 狂犬病 可以通过及时的伤口护理和 暴露后预防 来预防,但常规医院数据通常没有充分利用来确定当地的流行病学模式和预防重点。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对浙江大学医学院附属第二医院滨江院区的 38,537 条就诊记录进行了回顾性横断面分析。该数据集涵盖2017年1月1日至2020年10月27日。变量包括性别、年龄、初步诊断、分诊等级、暴露等级、暴露部位以及从分诊序列号得出的就诊日期。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用了描述性统计、Cramer V 的卡方检验和多变量逻辑回归。根据诊断关键词对暴露源和损伤机制进行分类。分析单位是访问记录。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在所有记录中,21,515 名(55.8%)为女性,平均年龄为 30.5 ± 14.4 岁。与猫相关的伤害占 19,137 条记录(49.7%),其次是与狗相关的伤害(16,844 条,43.7%)。咬伤和抓伤的比例几乎相同(分别为 19,025 例 [49.4%] 和 19,172 例 [49.7%])。在检查的变量中,暴露等级显示出与解剖部位最明显的关联,尽管效应大小很小(Cramer's V = 0.118,p. 11)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究详细描述了中国杭州一家大型城市医院中动物咬伤和抓伤的流行病学特征,并确定了与世界卫生组织 III 类接触相关的常规记录因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调动物咬伤和抓伤的最常见来源和部位,为当地的 狂犬病 预防策略提供信息,从而指导有针对性的干预措施和资源分配。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的数据缺失而受到限制,尤其是在 2020 年。该研究的证据是中等的,因为它依赖于常规医院记录,并且不包括 狂犬病病毒 的直接病毒学检测。

papers.title: A Correlational Study to Assess the Prevalence of Dog Bite Among Children and Awareness of Prevention and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Among Parents at Selected Community, Bangalore
papers.abstract: Dog bites are a major public health concern worldwide, especially in underdeveloped nations where rabies is still endemic. Rabies is a lethal viral disease transmitted mostly through dog bites that kill thousands of people each year, with children being the most vulnerable. "Rabies is a vaccine-preventable viral disease" that affect more than 150 countries and territories. Dogs are responsible for the great majority of human rabies deaths, accounting for up to 99% of rabies transmission to people. Objectives: Primary objectives1. To estimate the prevalence of dog bite among children.2. To assess the level of parental awareness regarding prevention of dog bites and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) among parents. Secondary objectives3. To assess the association between the prevalence of dog bites among children and selected demographic variables.4. To evaluate the association between parental awareness regarding prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis with selected demographic variables. Methodology: Study Design: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted to assess the epidemiological profile, management, and outcomes of dog bite cases. Study Setting: The study was carried out at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS, Data were collected from patients presenting with dog bites between [November, 2025to February 2026]
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

analysis.methods: The study design involved collecting data from patients presenting with dog bites at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS. The data collection period spanned from November 2025 to February 2026.
analysis.main_results: The study found that dogs are responsible for the great majority of human rabies deaths, accounting for up to 99% of rabies transmission to people.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the critical role of dog bites in rabies transmission and emphasized the need for increased awareness among parents regarding prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies aimed at reducing rabies transmission through dog bite prevention and improving parental awareness of post-exposure prophylaxis.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a descriptive cross-sectional analysis at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS to assess the prevalence of dog bites among children and parental awareness of prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis. The research highlighted that dogs are responsible for up to 99% of rabies transmission to humans, emphasizing the need for increased awareness among parents. The findings suggest that improving parental knowledge about rabies prevention and post-exposure measures could significantly impact public health outcomes. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis. The results underscore the importance of targeted interventions in communities where rabies remains endemic, particularly focusing on children and their caregivers.

analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,绝大多数人类死亡都是由狗造成的,占人类死亡的99%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了狗咬伤在 狂犬病 传播 中的关键作用,并强调需要提高家长对预防和 暴露后预防 的认识。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为旨在通过预防狗咬伤和提高家长对 暴露后预防 的认识来减少 狂犬病 传播 的公共卫生策略提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。证据是中等的,因为它提供了问题的描述性概述,但没有详细的统计分析。

papers.title: The Critical Need for a Comprehensive Post-Exposure Care Bundle following Rabies Exposure: A Report of Two Cases
papers.abstract: Rabies is a zoonotic disease that is almost always fatal but can be prevented; it disproportionately affects areas of Asia and Africa with limited resources. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) failures continue to cause avoidable deaths despite advancements in vaccination techniques. Two rabies deaths in which vaccination was not enough to prevent death are reported in the current study: one in an adult bitten by a wolf and another in a child bitten on the face by a stray dog. Critical shortcomings in comprehensive care, such as improper wound suturing, poor wound management, and a failure to administer rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), are highlighted in both cases. Both patients’ rabies infections were verified using histopathological and molecular analyses. These incidents underscore the crucial importance of a comprehensive “rabies care bundle” that encompasses active vaccination, passive immunization with RIG, and thorough wound care. To avoid similar results and preserve public trust in rabies vaccination programs, it is crucial to increase clinician awareness, ensure that all PEP components are accessible, and adhere to WHO guidelines.
papers.journal: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

papers.title: Longitudinal Assessment of Psychological Distress and Coping Strategies in Animal Bite Victims Undergoing Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis
papers.abstract: Animal bites, especially those from dogs, are a significant public health concern, leading to physical injuries and psychological distress. Rabies, a fatal zoonotic disease transmitted through dog bites, can be prevented by effective post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). The psychological impact, including anxiety and post-traumatic stress, is often neglected. The authors of the present study assessed psychological distress and coping responses among animal bite victims undergoing rabies PEP at multiple time points (days 0, 3, 7, and 28), using validated psychological scales to examine the influence of demographic and bite-related factors. A prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary care anti-rabies clinic in Northern India. Participants (≥12 years of age) with Category II or III animal bites were included. Data were collected through sociodemographic questionnaires and psychological assessments (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Impact of Event Scale–Revised [IES-R], Depression, Anxiety, Stress Scale [DASS-21], and Brief COPE). The sample size was 100 participants, accounting for a 20% nonresponse rate. Moderate to high anxiety levels were observed. Psychological distress, as measured via IES-R and DASS-21, decreased significantly over 28 days. Bite severity, age, and socioeconomic status influenced distress levels and coping strategies. Severe Category III bites were associated with higher anxiety and stress. The present study highlights the psychological burden of animal bites during rabies PEP, particularly severe dog bites. Psychological distress, including anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, and depression, improved over time, emphasizing the need for integrated psychological support in rabies PEP protocols, especially in resource-limited settings.
papers.journal: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

papers.title: Community knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding rabies prevention in Kédougou, Senegal, 2022
papers.abstract: Introduction: Rabies remains a public health problem in Senegal, particularly in the Kédougou region, where one rabies-related death was reported in 2019. The objective of this study was to analyse the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) of communities regarding rabies prevention. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Kédougou district using multistage cluster sampling (n = 845) recommended by WHO. A structured questionnaire was used to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics as well as rabies-related KAP, with a score cut-off of 80%. Frequencies and proportions were presented in tabular form, while odds ratios (ORs), p-values and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported for bivariate analysis. Variables with a p-value less than 0.20 were included in a logistic regression. Results: Among the 845 participants, 552 (65.3%) were male, with a median age of 40 years [18 to 67 years]. About 25.7% had good knowledge, 19.6% had positive attitudes, and 15.0% reported positive practices towards rabies. Community members who were rabies-aware (aOR = 5.57, CI: 2.46 – 15.1, p = 0.001) and males in the community (aOR = 2.54, CI: 1.27-5.65, p = 0.007) had better rabies preventive practices compared to those who were not rabies aware and their female counterparts. Conclusion: This study highlighted significant shortcomings in the KAPs in terms of rabies prevention. In order to reduce these gaps, awareness campaigns have been organised, focusing on the communication of the risks associated with this disease. It is therefore essential to design and implement a targeted communication plan geared towards the prevention and effective management of rabies.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:狂犬病 仍然是塞内加尔的一个公共卫生问题,特别是在凯杜古地区,2019 年报告了 1 例与 狂犬病 相关的死亡。本研究的目的是分析社区关于 狂犬病 预防的知识、态度和实践 (KAP)。方法:这项横断面研究是在凯杜古地区进行的,采用世界卫生组织推荐的多阶段整群抽样(n = 845)。使用结构化问卷收集社会人口特征以及 狂犬病 相关 KAP 的数据,分数截止值为 80%。频率和比例以表格形式呈现,而比值比 (OR)、p 值和 95% 置信区间 (CI) 则用于双变量分析。p 值小于 0.20 的变量包含在逻辑回归中。结果:845 名参与者中,552 名(65.3%)为男性,中位年龄为 40 岁[18 至 67 岁]。大约25.7%的人有良好的知识,19.6%的人有积极的态度,15.0%的人报告了对狂犬病的积极做法。与不了解 狂犬病 的社区成员及其女性相比,了解 狂犬病 的社区成员(aOR = 5.57,CI:2.46 – 15.1,p = 0.001)和社区中的男性(aOR = 2.54,CI:1.27-5.65,p = 0.007)具有更好的 狂犬病 预防措施同行。结论:本研究强调了 KAP 在 狂犬病 预防方面的显着缺陷。为了缩小这些差距,组织了宣传活动,重点是宣传与这种疾病相关的风险。因此,必须设计和实施旨在预防和有效管理 狂犬病 的有针对性的沟通计划。

This is the eleventh confirmed case of animal rabies in 2026. North Carolina law requires that all domestic pets (cats, dogs and ferrets), whether living inside or outside, aged four months or older be vaccinated for rabies. Animals that are confined in outdoor fenced areas should also have current rabies vaccinations. Supervising pets when they are outdoors could prevent contact with wild animals and lessen the possibility of rabies exposure. Guilford County Animal Services may be contacted for more information on rabies prevention at 336-641-2506 or visit our Animal Services website. For information regarding the current rabies cases, please contact Jorge Ortega at 336-641-3409 or jortega1@guilfordcountync.gov. Rabies circulates within our wildlife population throughout the entire year. Here are some tips to help prevent you or your family from being exposed to the rabies virus: Avoid direct contact with wildlife, dead or alive. Do not approach, try to play with, touch, rescue or treat any wildlife. If you find a sick or injured animal, contact Animal Control at 336-641-5990. Avoid any animal displaying unnatural behavior. Wild animals are not usually friendly so be very careful if they approach you. Do not try to separate fighting animals. Feed your pets indoors. Leaving food outside will attract dogs, cats and other wildlife into your yard. Report all stray animals to Animal Control at 336-641-5990 in Greensboro and 336-883-3224 in High Point. Stray animals may not have current rabies vaccinations. If a person is bitten by an animal (domestic or stray), wash the bitten area immediately with soap and water, seek medical attention, and report the bite to local Animal Control Officers. This is the eleventh confirmed case of animal rabies in 2026. North Carolina law requires that all domestic pets (cats, dogs and ferrets), whether living inside or outside, aged four months or older be vaccinated for rabies. Animals that are confined in outdoor fenced areas should also have current rabies vaccinations. Supervising pets when they are outdoors could prevent contact with wild animals and lessen the possibility of rabies exposure. Guilford County Animal Services may be contacted for more information on rabies prevention at 336-641-2506 or visit our Animal Services website. For information regarding the current rabies cases, please contact Jorge Ortega at 336-641-3409 or jortega1@guilfordcountync.gov. Rabies circulates within our wildlife population throughout the entire year. Here are some tips to help prevent you or your family from being exposed to the rabies virus: Avoid direct contact with wildlife, dead or alive. Do not approach, try to play with, touch, rescue or treat any wildlife. If you find a sick or injured animal, contact Animal Control at 336-641-5990. Avoid any animal displaying unnatural behavior. Wild animals are not usually friendly so be very careful if they approach you. Do not try to separate fighting animals. Feed your pets indoors. Leaving food outside will attract dogs, cats and other wildlife into your yard. Report all stray animals to Animal Control at 336-641-5990 in Greensboro and 336-883-3224 in High Point. Stray animals may not have current rabies vaccinations. If a person is bitten by an animal (domestic or stray), wash the bitten area immediately with soap and water, seek medical attention, and report the bite to local Animal Control Officers. news.content_title: Centre orders joint probes into every suspected human rabies death
news.content:
News Centre orders joint probes into every suspected human rabies death Priyanka Sharma 3 min read 5 Aug 2026, 06:22 PM IST Treating healthcare facilities must report every suspected rabies death on the Integrated Health Information Platform within 24 hours. Summary A new protocol mandates multi-agency investigations within 48 hours to trace infection sources, identify exposed contacts and strengthen rabies surveillance under the One Health framework. This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. India will, for the first time, investigate every suspected human rabies death through joint teams drawn from health, veterinary, municipal and forest departments, as the Centre moves to tighten surveillance and speed up containment amid persistent rabies fatalities. The National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has issued a standard operating procedure (SOP) mandating joint investigation teams at the national, state, district and block levels, according to two government officials and the document, Standard Operating Procedure for Joint Investigation of Suspected Human Rabies Deaths , reviewed by Mint . The protocol aims to confirm rabies deaths, trace the animal source, identify exposed contacts and ensure timely vaccination. Local authorities must begin field investigations within 48 hours of notification and submit final investigation reports within seven days. Also Read | India looks to overhaul disease outbreak response with a regional push One Health response The framework adopts the One Health approach, bringing together the departments of health and family welfare, animal husbandry and dairying, urban and rural local bodies, forest and wildlife, and designated rabies diagnostic laboratories. Treating healthcare facilities must report every suspected rabies death on the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) within 24 hours. Joint investigation teams will then collect medical records, interview family members and caregivers, map bite locations, and assess whether anti-rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins were administered appropriately, according to the SOP. Primary healthcare officers will also review vaccine storage, procurement and distribution at regional healthcare facilities. Rabies, a preventable yet almost invariably fatal viral disease once symptoms appear, remains a major public health challenge. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), dogs account for nearly 96% of human rabies cases worldwide, with the remaining 4% linked to bites from cats, monkeys, mongooses, wild cats and cattle. Government data shows dog-bite cases rose to 3.72 million in 2024 from 2.75 million a year earlier, while rabies deaths climbed to 180 from 22 in 2022, prompting a new SOP for multi-agency investigations and faster containment. Queries sent to the health ministry spokesperson remained unanswered until press time. Also Read | Data gaps stall Bharat Biotech's TB vaccine trial plans From investigation to containment Animal investigations will survey exposure sites to trace, isolate and observe dogs, livestock or wild animals linked to bite incidents. The SOP directs field investigators collecting biological specimens to use personal protective equipment, including double gloves and masks, while maintaining specimens at two to eight degrees Celsius during transport. Designated laboratories will test brain tissue or saliva samples using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and direct fluorescent antibody tests, sharing results with health departments within 24-48 hours. Local teams must submit final reports within seven days, documenting the likely transmission route, community risks and preventive measures. Where wild animals such as jackals, foxes or feral cats are suspected sources, forest departments will lead field operations and establish a 5-km buffer zone around the exposure site. Teams will carry out targeted animal vaccination, monitor wildlife morbidity, conduct door-to-door risk assessments in nearby villages and manage local waste to reduce human-wildlife interactions. Exposed contacts will receive post-exposure vaccines and rabies immunoglobulins immediately, without waiting for laboratory confirmation. The framework also mandates monthly data sharing across state and district departments, including confirmed rabies deaths, dog-bite clusters, stray dog census data, vaccinated and neutered animal counts, and anti-rabies vaccine stock levels. Affected areas will remain under surveillance for six months to assess response measures, vaccination coverage and future prevention efforts. Why coordination matters The multi-sectoral push comes as rising dog-bite incidents increase demand for vaccination across human healthcare and veterinary sectors. Industry estimates value India's veterinary rabies vaccine market at $37.6 million, with projections of $56.8 million by 2030 as municipal bodies and pet owners expand preventive vaccination. Dr Rajeev Jayadevan, a public health expert said, “Rabies is virtually 100% fatal once the infection reaches the central nervous system. But it is also preventable on many fronts...In many developed countries, rabies from dog bites has been eliminated. While dog bites are still common, human rabies does not occur because the virus no longer circulates among pet dogs in these countries.” Also Read | Inside food companies’ scramble to dial back health claims Jayadevan said rabies originated as a zoonotic spillover, with the virus spreading from forest animals to free-roaming stray dogs along forest fringes before reaching other stray and pet dogs and cats in both rural and urban areas, where it continues to circulate. He added that controlling and eliminating human rabies in India would require a coordinated, multi-pronged approach backed by swift tracking and accountability. About the Author Priyanka Sharma Priyanka Sharma is a journalist at Mint, where she covers the Union Ministry of Health and the pharmaceutical industry. Her work focuses on explaining government policies and how they impact healthcare and the medicine market in India. With 12 years of experience in journalism, she has built a reputation for providing clear and honest news on important health topics that affect the entire country.

Her educational background includes a journalism degree from the prestigious Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) and specialized training in public health from the Public Health Foundation of India. Before her current role at Mint, Priyanka worked with India Today, The Pioneer, and ANI. She also served as a lead consultant for the National Health Authority, which gave her firsthand knowledge of how the government manages large-scale health programmes.

Priyanka is based in New Delhi and is an avid traveller who loves visiting the mountains. She has a great interest in regional flavours, particularly South Indian food. Stay updated with the latest Trending , India , World and US news. More Topics # Public Health # healthcare

news.content: Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global EditionASIA 中文双语Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE Business Macro Companies Industries Technology Motoring China Data Finance Top 10 Home / Business / Companies Home Business Companies Sinovac gets approval for China's first serum-free rabies vaccine By Li Jing | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-08-06 16:42 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Chinese vaccine maker Sinovac Biotech said on Thursday it had received regulatory approval for a freeze-dried human rabies vaccine that uses a serum-free, animal component-free manufacturing process and supports a shortened four-dose vaccination schedule recommended by the World Health Organization. The vaccine received a drug registration certificate from the National Medical Products Administration, the company said in a statement. Sinovac said the product is China's first serum-free rabies vaccine approved for both the conventional five-dose regimen and the WHO-recommended "abridged" four-dose schedule for post-exposure prophylaxis. The four-dose regimen requires injections on days 0, 3, 7 and between days 14 and 28, allowing the primary vaccination course to be completed in as little as 14 days. Rabies is a viral disease that is almost invariably fatal once symptoms develop, making timely vaccination after exposure critical. Sinovac said it has also begun overseas development of the vaccine, including a product development partnership with the government of Brazil and multiple international clinical studies in Pakistan. news.content: Community Corner Free Rabies Clinic Set For Brookhaven Animal Shelter On Saturday The clinic is available to all Suffolk County residents, but quantity is limited, and vaccines are available while supplies last. Peggy Spellman Hoey , Patch Staff Posted Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 9:12 am ET Read More BROOKHAVEN, NY — The Suffolk County Department of Health Services is joining Brookhaven Town to offer free rabies vaccinations for dogs, cats, and ferrets on Saturday at the Animal Shelter and Adoption Center. The event will run from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Although the clinic is available to all county residents, quantity is limited, and vaccines are available while supplies last. Find out what's happening in Patchogue for free with the latest updates from Patch. No appointment is needed. All dogs must be on a leash, and all cats and ferrets must be in carriers. Find out what's happening in Patchogue for free with the latest updates from Patch. Rabies, a deadly disease caused by a virus that attacks the central nervous system, is most often seen among wild animals such as raccoons, bats, skunks and foxes, but any mammal can be infected with rabies. Pets and livestock can get rabies if they are not vaccinated to protect them against infection. New York State and Suffolk County laws require that all dogs, cats and ferrets be vaccinated against rabies. Vaccinating pets not only provides protection for the animals but also acts as a barrier to keep the rabies virus from spreading between wild animals and people. Three to six percent of bats tested annually are positive for rabies. Suffolk's Department of Health Services recommends the following precautions to protect pets and families from possible exposure to rabies: Do not feed, touch, or approach wild animals, or stray dogs or cats. Be sure your pet dogs, cats, and ferrets as well as horses and other livestock animals are up to date on their rabies vaccinations. Pets too young to be vaccinated should be kept indoors and allowed outside only under direct observation. Keep family pets indoors at night. Do not leave them outside unattended or let them roam free. Do not attract wild animals to your home or yard. Keep your property free of stored bird seed or other foods that may attract wild animals. Feed pets indoors. Tightly cover or put away garbage cans. Board up any openings to your attic, basement, porch or garage. Cap your chimney with screens. Do not transport or relocate any wild animals. Teach children not to touch any animal they do not know and to tell an adult immediately if they are bitten by any animal. Techniques to keep bats from getting into buildings include: Not leaving unscreened doors or windows open to the outside Making sure windows have screens, chimneys are capped, and electrical and plumbing openings are plugged Sealing openings larger than 1/2 inch Using materials such as expanding spray-on foam, caulk, wire mesh, wood that fits tightly, steel wool (around pipes that enter buildings), or polypropylene bird netting, to seal or cover gaps and holes Report all animal bites or contact with wild animals to the Department of Health at 631-854-0333 weekdays from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or 631-852-4820 outside business hours. If possible, try to contain the animal so that it can be tested. Get more local news delivered straight to your inbox. Sign up for free Patch newsletters and alerts

By WBAY news staff Published: Aug. 4, 2026 at 11:42 AM UTC Share Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google WINNEBAGO COUNTY, Wis. (WBAY) - While tornado cleanup continues in Menasha, health officials are issuing a new warning about stray animals. People are urged not to approach or handle stray or feral cats or other animals roaming the storm-damaged areas. Officials say recent incidents forced some people to get rabies vaccinations -- a treatment that’s expensive and avoidable. Stray animals may carry diseases that pose serious health risks, and may be more likely to scratch or bite when they’re stressed or hurt after a tornado. People should not feed, capture or move these animals. Instead, call local animal control or police if you see one so professionals can respond and capture the animal safely. Copyright 2026 WBAY. analysis.brief_en: In Winnebago County, Wisconsin, health officials have warned residents to avoid interacting with stray or feral animals in tornado-affected areas. Following recent incidents, some individuals have been vaccinated for rabies, a costly and preventable measure. The warning highlights the risk of disease transmission from these animals, especially as they may be stressed or injured after the storm. Officials advise against feeding, capturing, or moving the animals and recommend contacting local animal control or police for safe handling. This guidance aims to prevent unnecessary exposure and ensure public safety during the cleanup process.

(Maryland Department of Natural Resources) 0Comment Share topics: Rabies Cunningham Falls State Park Beaver Maryland Department of Health Frederick County Health Department Rabies exposure Park closures Health advisory THURMONT, Md. (WBFF) — A beaver that attacked a 19-year-old fisherman in Cunningham Falls State Park on Aug. 5 tested positive for rabies, the Maryland Department of Health confirmed Thursday. This is the second beaver to test positive for the rabies virus at the state park within the past two weeks. “Rabies can infect mammals through a bite or a scratch. Once an animal or person starts showing symptoms, it is almost always fatal unless treatment is given,” said Barry Glotfelty, Director for Frederick County Health Department’s Environmental Health Services. As this time, officials have closed The Houck day use area, boat ramp, and the Big Hunting Creek above the lake. All use of the closed areas is prohibited until the area can be confirmed safe for visitors. The effort is expected to take several days, said officials. analysis.brief_en: A second beaver at Cunningham Falls State Park in Maryland has tested positive for rabies, according to the Maryland Department of Health. This follows a previous incident on July 26, 2026, where a teenager was bitten by a beaver in the park's swimming area, and the animal tested positive for rabies on July 27, 2026. In response, officials have closed the Houck day use area, boat ramp, and Big Hunting Creek above the lake to the public. These closures are in place until the area is confirmed safe, which is expected to take several days. The Maryland Department of Health is urging anyone who has been bitten or scratched by a beaver in the park to contact their healthcare provider and the Frederick County Health Department’s Community Health Services Office at 301-600-3342. The rabies virus is a serious concern, as it is almost always fatal once symptoms appear unless treated promptly. This event highlights the importance of public health advisories and the need for vigilance in areas where rabies exposure is possible.

This event highlights the importance of public health advisories and the need for vigilance in areas where rabies exposure is possible.
